newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech securities centre postpones fee changes.
newsitem.headline: Czech securities centre postpones fee changes.

text.p: The Czech Central Securities Registry (SCP) said on Thursday that it had indefinitely postponed plans to change its method of charging transaction fees due to be implemented on August 1.
"The SCP announces that from a decision of the Ministry of Finance, it is postponing the realisation of the new methods of charging for securities transactions," an SCP statement said.
"The charge for services at the SCP, that is to say, are remaining unchanged after August 1, 1997," it added.
The main change proposed by the SCP was to be the implementation of a fee equal to 0.5 percent of the turnover of each trade on securities transactions performed off organised markets.
The statement said the original proposals had been postponed because of changes in transaction fees on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) announced recently which made changes at the SCP superfluous.
The PSE said that it would charge a percentage of the turnover involved in direct trades.
Subsequently, however, the PSE said the charges would be subject to an upper limit depending on which market the shares are listed on, ranging from 500 crowns to an absolute maximum of 5,000 crowns.
The new fee had been intended to come amid a total overhaul of charges assessed by the state-controlled SCP.

Czech government officials and market participants have taken steps recently to encourage more trading to take place on the country's two organised markets -- the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) and the retail-oriented RM-System.
The PSE has imposed a ban on its members trading shares of companies listed on its main and parallel markets outside of the two organised markets from August 1.
A large majority of turnover in Czech securities has been concentrated in direct trades which have been simply registered at the SCP.
Analysts say that this practice has drained the market of liquidity and transparency.
